requirement:
`ValidationCache::usage()` returns an owned snapshot of the cache’s lifetime
{cite}`requirements.sdk.graph.running-criteria.UsageStats`. A newly constructed
cache starts at zero. Every agent call through the cache or any clone adds its
usage exactly once by the time the call returns, including retries and failed
attempts. Concurrent calls contribute to the same totals. The snapshot sums tool invocations and result bytes by tool name across validators under {cite}`requirements.sdk.graph.running-criteria.ToolUsage.by_name`. Reading a snapshot
preserves the counters, and later calls leave earlier snapshots unchanged.

```rust,ignore
impl<D: Domain> ValidationCache<D> {
    pub fn usage(&self) -> UsageStats;
}
```
rationale:
The tests marked for `requirements.sdk.validation-cache.usage` cover each obligation in its text. All of them are in `crates/trust-but-verify/src/agent/tests.rs`.

- **Zero start.** `fn[agent_executions_isolate_conversations_and_dependency_traces]` takes `cache.usage()` before any call. It asserts that `initial.tools` is empty and that `initial.attempts` is 0. The cache snapshot does not check every counter. `fn[validators_keep_measured_tokens_after_failed_attempts_and_evidence_reuse]` checks every field, including all five token categories, but only on a fresh `Validator`'s usage. The rest of the cache snapshot is a minor, low-risk gap.
- **Counted exactly once, through any clone.** `fn[cache_retains_usage_across_validators_and_sums_each_token_category]` runs two validators on `graph` and its clone `peer`. `graph.cache()`, `peer.cache()` and a retained `cache` clone all report 3 attempts. Totals are 1 retry, 1 failed attempt, token sums of 19, 13, 5, 3 and 8, and `missing_attempts` of 1. Summing tokens across calls shows that each call contributed exactly once.
- **Retries and failed attempts.** The same test includes a throttled first attempt that is retried. `fn[validators_keep_measured_tokens_after_failed_attempts_and_evidence_reuse]` has a throttled attempt, a success, then a terminal failure. It asserts attempts, retries and failed_attempts of (3, 1, 2) on `graph.cache().usage()`. `fn[dropping_an_inflight_request_preserves_its_attempt]` shows that a dropped in-flight request still counts as one attempt on the cache.
- **Concurrency.** `fn[agent_executions_isolate_conversations_and_dependency_traces]` runs two executions concurrently, synchronized by a `Barrier`. The cache totals are 6 attempts and per-tool calls of 2, equal to the sum of the two validators. That rules out lost or double-counted updates.
- **Tool sums by name across validators.** The same test checks `read_node`, `get_next_page` and `submit_result`. For each name, cache `calls` is 2 and `result_bytes` equals the sum of the two validators' `result_bytes`. It also asserts that the cache has exactly three tool entries.
- **Snapshots are owned and unchanged.** `fn[agent_executions_isolate_conversations_and_dependency_traces]` takes `initial` before the runs and asserts `initial.attempts == 0` afterwards. `fn[validators_keep_measured_tokens_after_failed_attempts_and_evidence_reuse]` takes `before_failure` and asserts `before_failure.failed_attempts == 1` after the later failure raised the live totals to 2. Both show that later calls leave earlier snapshots unchanged. Repeated `usage()` reads return consistent values, so reading preserves the counters.

The cited `requirements.sdk.graph.running-criteria.UsageStats` and `requirements.sdk.graph.running-criteria.ToolUsage.by_name` are covered here in the subject's case. Prepared and delivered inputs are checked on the cache in two tests. Tool maps are checked on the cache with built-in tools. I did not review the unmarked tests that read `cache().usage()` with registered tools. Registered-tool coverage is not required here, because the built-in tools go through the same per-name summing.

`public_exports_match_the_appendix` only checks that the public API is exported. It adds no behavioral coverage, and none is needed from it.

I found no unacknowledged gap.

text: `ValidationCache::usage()` returns an owned snapshot of the cache’s lifetime
cache starts at zero. Every agent call through the cache or any clone adds its
usage exactly once by the time the call returns, including retries and failed

attempts. Concurrent calls contribute to the same totals. The snapshot sums tool invocations and result bytes by tool name across validators under {cite}`requirements.sdk.graph.running-criteria.ToolUsage.by_name`. Reading a snapshot
preserves the counters, and later calls leave earlier snapshots unchanged.

`UsageStats` exposes the following totals. `attempts` counts each request sent to the provider once. `retries` counts attempts that repeat a failed request. `failed_attempts` counts attempts that returned a provider error, including those followed by a successful retry.

`prepared_inputs` counts inputs prepared for agent messages. Each node inserted in the opening message counts once. Each requested `read_node` page and each `outgoing_edges` result counts once, including repeated reads. A requested search page counts one input per excerpt on that page. Source listings, search finalization, and opaque custom-tool results contribute zero.

`delivered_inputs` counts those inputs when the provider first responds successfully to the request carrying them. Each input counts once across retries and subsequent turns that replay the same conversation history. For example, if the opening message supplies three nodes and the provider fails permanently before replying, usage records three prepared inputs and zero delivered inputs.
`UsageStats::tools` starts empty and holds one entry per invoked tool, keyed by name. This includes built-in and registered tools.
